vsm2.12:69.1: He appears and vanishes: the meaning here is that he causes appearance, causes vanishing.
vsm2.12:69.2:
For it is said in the Paṭisambhidā with reference to this: “‘He appears’: he is not veiled by something, he is not hidden,
he is revealed, he is evident. ‘Vanishes’: he is veiled by something, he is hidden, he is shut away, he is enclosed” (Paṭis II 207).
vsm2.12:69.3:
Now, this possessor of supernormal power who wants to make an appearance, makes darkness into light, or he makes
revealed what is hidden, or he makes what has not come into the visual field come into the visual field.
vsm2.12:70.2:
If he wants to make himself or another visible even though hidden or at a distance, he emerges from the basic
jhāna and adverts thus, “Let this that is dark become light” or “Let this that is hidden be revealed” or “Let
this that has not come into the visual field come into the visual field.”
vsm2.12:70.3: Then he does the preliminary work and resolves in the way already described.
vsm2.12:70.4: It becomes as resolved simultaneously with the resolve.
vsm2.12:70.5: Others then see even when at a distance; and he himself sees too, if he wants to see.
vsm2.12:71.1: But by whom was this miracle formerly performed?
vsm2.12:71.3:
For when the Blessed One had been invited by Cūḷa-Subhaddā and was traversing the seven-league journey between
Sāvatthī and Sāketa with five hundred palanquins created by Vissakamma (see Dhp-a III 470), he resolved in suchwise
that citizens of Sāketa saw the inhabitants of Sāvatthī and citizens of Sāvatthī saw the inhabitants of Sāketa.
vsm2.12:71.4:
And when he had alighted in the centre of the city, he split the earth in two and showed
Avīci, and he parted the sky in two and showed the Brahmā-world.
vsm2.12:72.1: And this meaning should also be explained by means of the Descent of the Gods (devorohaṇa).
vsm2.12:72.2:
When the Blessed One, it seems, had performed the Twin Miracle and had liberated eighty-four thousand beings from bonds,
he wondered, “Where did the past Enlightened Ones go to when they had finished the Twin Miracle?”
vsm2.12:72.3: He saw that they had gone to the heaven of the Thirty-three.
vsm2.12:72.4: Then he stood with one foot on the surface of the earth, and placed the second on Mount Yugandhara.
vsm2.12:72.5: Then again he lifted his first foot and set it on the summit of Mount Sineru.
vsm2.12:72.6:
He took up the residence for the Rains there on the Red Marble Terrace, and he began his exposition of the Abhidhamma,
starting from the beginning, to the deities of ten thousand world-spheres.
vsm2.12:72.7: At the time for wandering for alms he created an artificial Buddha to teach the Dhamma.
vsm2.12:73.1: Meanwhile the Blessed One himself would chew a tooth-stick of nāgalatā wood and wash his mouth in Lake Anotatta.
vsm2.12:73.2: Then, after collecting alms food among the Uttarakurus, he would eat it on the shores of that lake.
vsm2.12:73.3:
Each day the Elder Sāriputta went there and paid homage to the Blessed One, who told him,
“Today I taught this much Dhamma,” and he gave him the method.
vsm2.12:73.4: In this way he gave an uninterrupted exposition of the Abhidhamma for three months.
vsm2.12:73.5: Eighty million deities penetrated the Dhamma on hearing it.
vsm2.12:74.1: At the time of the Twin Miracle an assembly gathered that was twelve leagues across.
vsm2.12:74.2: Then, saying, “We will disperse when we have seen the Blessed One,” they made an encampment and waited there.
vsm2.12:74.3: Anāthapiṇḍika the Lesser supplied all their needs.
vsm2.12:74.4: People asked the Elder Anuruddha to find out where the Blessed One was.
vsm2.12:74.5: The elder extended light, and with the divine eye he saw where the Blessed One had taken up residence for the Rains.
vsm2.12:74.6: As soon as he saw this, he announced it.
vsm2.12:75.1: They asked the venerable Mahā Moggallāna to pay homage to the Blessed One.
vsm2.12:75.2: In the midst of the assembly the elder dived into the earth.
vsm2.12:75.3: Then cleaving Mount Sineru, he emerged at the Perfect One’s feet, and he paid homage at the Blessed One’s feet.
vsm2.12:75.4:
This is what he told the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the inhabitants of Jambudīpa pay homage at the Blessed
One’s feet, and they say, ‘We will disperse when we have seen the Blessed One.’”
vsm2.12:75.5: The Blessed One said, “But, Moggallāna, where is your elder brother, the General of the Dhamma?”—
vsm2.12:75.6: “At the city of Saṅkassa, venerable sir.”—
vsm2.12:75.7:
“Moggallāna, those who wish to see me should come tomorrow to the city of Saṅkassa. Tomorrow being the Uposatha
day of the full moon, I shall descend to the city of Saṅkassa for the Mahāpavāraṇā ceremony.”
vsm2.12:76.1:
Saying, “Good, venerable sir,” the elder paid homage to Him of the Ten
Powers, and descending by the way he came, he reached the human neighbourhood.
vsm2.12:76.2: And at the time of his going and coming he resolved that people should see it.
vsm2.12:76.3: This, firstly, is the miracle of becoming apparent that the Elder Mahā Moggallāna performed here.
vsm2.12:76.4:
Having arrived thus, he related what had happened, and he said, “Come forth after the morning meal and pay
no heed to distance” thus promising that they would be able to see in spite of the distance.
vsm2.12:77.1: The Blessed One informed Sakka, Ruler of Gods, “Tomorrow, O King, I am going to the human world.”
vsm2.12:77.2:
The Ruler of Gods commanded Vissakamma, “Good friend, the Blessed One wishes to go to the human world tomorrow.
Build three flights of stairs, one of gold, one of silver and one of crystal.”
vsm2.12:78.1: On the following day the Blessed One stood on the summit of Sineru and surveyed the eastward world element.
vsm2.12:78.2: Many thousands of world-spheres were visible to him as clearly as a single plain.
vsm2.12:78.3: And as the eastward world element, so too he saw the westward, the northward and the southward world elements all clearly visible.
vsm2.12:78.4:
And he saw right down to Avīci, and up to the Realm of the Highest Gods. That day, it seems, was called
the day of the Revelation of Worlds (loka-vivaraṇa). Human beings saw deities, and deities saw human beings. And in doing
so the human beings did not have to look up or the deities down. They all saw each other face to face.
vsm2.12:79.1:
The Blessed One descended by the middle flight of stairs made of crystal; the deities of the six sense-sphere heavens by that on
the left side made of gold; and the deities of the Pure Abodes, and the Great Brahmā, by that on the right side made of silver.
vsm2.12:79.2: The Ruler of Gods held the bowl and robe.
vsm2.12:79.3: The Great Brahmā held a three-league-wide white parasol.
vsm2.12:79.5:
Five-crest (Pañcasikha), the son of the gandhabba, descended doing honour to the Blessed
One with his bael-wood lute measuring three quarters of a league.
vsm2.12:79.6: On that day there was no living being present who saw the Blessed One but yearned for enlightenment.
vsm2.12:79.7: This is the miracle of becoming apparent that the Blessed One performed here.
vsm2.12:80.1:
Furthermore, in Tambapaṇṇi Island (Sri Lanka), while the Elder Dhammadinna, resident of Taḷaṅgara, was sitting on the shrine
terrace in the Great Monastery of Tissa (Tissamahāvihāra) expounding the Apaṇṇaka Sutta, “Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu possesses three
things he enters upon the untarnished way” (A I 113), he turned his fan face downwards and an opening right down to Avīci appeared.
vsm2.12:80.2: Then he turned it face upwards and an opening right up to the Brahmā-world appeared.
vsm2.12:80.3: Having thus aroused fear of hell and longing for the bliss of heaven, the elder taught the Dhamma.
vsm2.12:80.4: Some became stream-enterers, some once-returners, some non-returners, some Arahants.
vsm2.12:81.1:
But one who wants to cause a vanishing makes light into darkness, or he hides what is unbidden, or he
makes what has come into the visual field come no more into the visual field.
vsm2.12:81.3:
If he wants to make himself or another invisible even though unconcealed or nearby, he emerges from the basic
jhāna and adverts thus, “Let this light become darkness” or “Let this that is unhidden be hidden” or “Let
this that has come into the visual field not come into the visual field.”
vsm2.12:81.4: Then he does the preliminary work and resolves in the way already described.
vsm2.12:81.5: It becomes as he has resolved simultaneously with the resolution.
vsm2.12:81.6: Others do not see even when they are nearby.
vsm2.12:81.7: He too does not see, if he does not want to see.
vsm2.12:82.1: But by whom was this miracle formerly performed?
vsm2.12:82.3: For the Blessed One so acted that when the clansman Yasa was sitting beside him, his father did not see him (Vin I 16).
vsm2.12:82.4:
Likewise, after travelling two thousand leagues to meet King Mahā Kappina and establishing
him in the fruition of non-return and his thousand ministers in the fruition of stream-entry,
vsm2.12:82.5:
he so acted that Queen Anojā, who had followed the king with a thousand women
attendants and was sitting nearby, did not see the king and his retinue.
vsm2.12:82.6: And when he was asked, “Have you seen the king, venerable sir?,”
vsm2.12:82.7: he asked, “But which is better for you, to seek the king or to seek your self?” (cf. Vin I 23).
vsm2.12:82.9:
Then he likewise taught her the Dhamma as she sat there, so that, together with the thousand women
attendants, she became established in the fruition of stream-entry, while the ministers reached
the fruition of non-return, and the king that of Arahantship (see A-a I 322; Dhp-a II 124).
vsm2.12:83.1:
Furthermore, this was performed by the Elder Mahinda, who so acted on the day of his arrival in Tambapaṇṇi
Island that the king did not see the others who had come with him (see Mahāvaṃsa I 103).
vsm2.12:84.1: Furthermore, all miracles of making evident are called an appearance,
vsm2.12:84.2: and all miracles of making unevident are called a vanishing.
vsm2.12:84.3: Herein, in the miracle of making evident, both the supernormal power and the possessor of the supernormal power are displayed.
vsm2.12:84.4: That can be illustrated with the Twin Miracle; for in that both are displayed thus:
vsm2.12:84.5: “Here the Perfect One performs the Twin Miracle, which is not shared by disciples.
vsm2.12:84.6: He produces a mass of fire from the upper part of his body and a shower of water from the lower part of his body …” (Paṭis I 125).
vsm2.12:84.7: In the case of the miracle of making unevident, only the supernormal power is displayed, not the possessor of the supernormal power.
vsm2.12:84.8: That can be illustrated by means of the Mahaka Sutta (S IV 200), and the Brahmanimantanika Sutta (M I 330).
vsm2.12:84.9:
For there it was only the supernormal power of the venerable Mahaka and of the Blessed One respectively
that was displayed, not the possessors of the supernormal power, according as it is said:
vsm2.12:85.1: “When he had sat down at one side, the householder Citta said to the venerable Mahaka,
vsm2.12:85.2: ‘Venerable sir, it would be good if the lord would show me a miracle of supernormal power belonging to the higher than human state.’
vsm2.12:85.3: — ‘Then, householder, spread your upper robe out on the terrace and scatter a bundle of hay on it.’
vsm2.12:85.4:
—‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the householder replied to the venerable Mahaka, and he spread out
his upper robe on the terrace and scattered a bundle of hay on it.
vsm2.12:85.5: Then the venerable Mahaka went into his dwelling and fastened the latch, after which he performed a feat of supernormal power
vsm2.12:85.6:
such that flames came out from the keyhole and from the gaps in the fastenings and burned
the hay without burning the upper robe” (S IV 290).
vsm2.12:86.1: Also according as it is said:
vsm2.12:86.2: “Then, bhikkhus, I performed a feat of supernormal power
vsm2.12:86.3:
such that Brahmā and Brahmā’s retinue, and those attached to Brahmā’s retinue might hear
my voice and yet not see me, and having vanished in this way,
vsm2.12:86.5:
I saw the fear in all kinds of becoming, Including becoming that seeks non-becoming; And no becoming
do I recommend; I cling to no delight therein at all (M I 330).
vsm2.12:87.1: He goes unhindered through walls, through enclosures, through mountains, as though in open space:
vsm2.12:87.2: here through walls is beyond walls; the yonder side of a wall, is what is meant.
vsm2.12:87.4: And wall is a term for the wall of a house;
vsm2.12:87.5: enclosure is a wall surrounding a house, monastery (park), village, etc.;
vsm2.12:87.6: mountain is a mountain of soil or a mountain of stone.
vsm2.12:87.8: As though in open space: just as if he were in open space.
vsm2.12:88.1: One who wants to go in this way should attain the space-kasiṇa jhāna and emerge,
vsm2.12:88.2:
and then do the preliminary work by adverting to the wall or the enclosure or some
such mountain as Sineru or the World-sphere Mountains,
vsm2.12:88.3: and he should resolve, “Let there be space.”
vsm2.12:88.5: it becomes hollow for him if he wants to go down or up;
vsm2.12:88.6: it becomes cleft for him if he wants to penetrate it.
vsm2.12:89.1: But here the Elder Tipiṭaka Cūḷa-Abhaya said:
vsm2.12:89.2: “Friends, what is the use of attaining the space-kasiṇa jhāna?
vsm2.12:89.3: Does one who wants to create elephants, horses, etc., attain an elephant-kasiṇa jhāna or horse-kasiṇa jhāna, and so on?
vsm2.12:89.4: Surely the only standard is mastery in the eight attainments,
vsm2.12:89.5: and after the preliminary work has been done on any kasiṇa, it then becomes whatever he wishes.”
vsm2.12:89.7: “Venerable sir, only the space kasiṇa has been given in the text, so it should certainly be mentioned.”
vsm2.12:90.2: “He is normally an obtainer of the space-kasiṇa attainment.
vsm2.12:90.3: He adverts: “Through the wall, through the enclosure, through the mountain.
vsm2.12:90.4: Having adverted, he resolves with knowledge: “Let there be space.”
vsm2.12:90.6: He goes unhindered through the wall, through the enclosure, through the mountain.
vsm2.12:90.7: Just as men normally not possessed of supernormal power go unhindered where there is no obstruction or enclosure,
vsm2.12:90.8:
so too this possessor of supernormal power, by his attaining mental mastery, goes unhindered through the wall,
through the enclosure, through the mountain, as though in open space” (Paṭis II 208).
vsm2.12:91.1:
What if a mountain or a tree is raised in this bhikkhu’s way while he is travelling
along after resolving; should he attain and resolve again?
vsm2.12:91.2: There is no harm in that.
vsm2.12:91.3: For attaining and resolving again is like taking the dependence (see Vin I 58; II 274) in the preceptor’s presence.
vsm2.12:91.4: And because this bhikkhu has resolved, “Let there be space,” there will be only space there,
vsm2.12:91.5:
and because of the power of his first resolve it is impossible that another mountain or tree
can have sprung up meanwhile made by temperature.
vsm2.12:91.6: However, if it has been created by another possessor of supernormal power and created first, it prevails;
vsm2.12:91.7: the former must go above or below it.
vsm2.12:92.1: He dives in and out of the ground (pathaviyā pi ummujjanimmujjaṃ):
vsm2.12:92.2: here it is rising up that is called “diving out” (ummujja)
vsm2.12:92.3: and it is sinking down that is called “diving in” (nimmujja).
vsm2.12:92.4: Ummujjanimmujjaṃ = ummujjañ ca nimmujjañ ca (resolution of compound).
vsm2.12:92.5: One who wants to do this should attain the water-kasiṇa jhāna and emerge.
vsm2.12:92.6:
Then he should do the preliminary work, determining thus, “Let the earth in such an area
be water,” and he should resolve in the way already described.
vsm2.12:92.7: Simultaneously with the resolve, that much extent of earth according as determined becomes water only.
vsm2.12:92.8: It is there he does the diving in and out.
